extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, and librarians seeking information about the MathSciNet bibliographic database
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and summarize the functional/selection/coverage policies and quality-related features of the MathSciNet bibliographic database as described on its Wikipedia page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the database is by subscription only and is not generally available to individual researchers who are not affiliated with a larger subscribing institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that MathSciNet is a paywalled service (institutional subscriptions are the normal access route) and not freely available to unaffiliated individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Mathematical Reviews contents
rubrics_metrics.description: It contains all of the contents of the journal Mathematical Reviews (MR) since 1940 along with an extensive author database, links to other MR entries, citations, full journal entries, and links to original articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathSciNet aims to mirror MR content comprehensively (back to 1940) and to provide bibliographic linkage (MR entries, citations, links to originals) plus an author database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and coverage breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: MathSciNet contains information on over 3 million articles and over eight hundred thousand authors indexed from 1800 mathematical journals, many of them abstracted 'cover-to-cover'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates large-scale coverage (millions of items, hundreds of thousands of authors) and that many journals are fully abstracted rather than selectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference List Journals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A portion of those journals (about 450 in 2012) are designated as 'Reference List Journals'; for MathSciNet entries of papers from these journals original reference lists are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For designated Reference List Journals, MathSciNet includes the original reference lists in entries, improving bibliographic completeness for those sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of selected applied-journal content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews or bibliographical information on selected articles is included from many engineering, computer science and other applied journals abstracted by MathSciNet. The selection is done by the editors of Mathematical Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied-discipline journals are not all automatically included cover-to-cover; editors choose which applied-journal articles or items to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection and suggestion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors accept suggestions to cover additional journals, but do not reconsider missing articles for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial process: users may suggest journals for coverage, but the editors will not retroactively add individual missing articles — selection is forward-looking at the journal level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification and disambiguation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike most other abstracting databases, MathSciNet takes care to uniquely identify authors. Its author search allows the user to find publications associated with a given author record, even if multiple authors have exactly the same name or if the same person publishes under multiple names or name variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathSciNet maintains distinct author records and actively disambiguates name variants; Mathematical Reviews personnel may even contact authors to ensure correct attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-development of subject classification
rubrics_metrics.description: MathSciNet co-develops the Mathematics Subject Classification taxonomy with zbMATH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathSciNet uses and helps maintain the MSC taxonomy for subject classification of mathematical literature, which underpins how items are categorized and searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of bibliographic links and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: It contains almost 3.6 million items and over 2.3 million links to original articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathSciNet emphasizes linking entries to original articles and providing comprehensive metadata to facilitate locating source works.
